business.title: Development of an automated method for audiometric data extraction and analysis using voting optical character recognition
business.desc: Hearing loss affects over 1.5 billion people worldwide, significantly impacting language development, quality of life, and economic independence. Research on audiometric data, such as pure tone audiometry (PTA), the speech reception threshold (SRT), and the word recognition score (WRS), is essential for understanding and preventing hearing loss. However, this data is frequently stored as image files within electronic medical records (EMRs), thus requiring manual extraction for research use. Manual extraction is time-consuming, costly, and prone to errors, limiting data utility and impeding large-scale data acquisition. In this paper, we propose an automated extraction method for audiometric report images using Tesseract optical character recognition (OCR) and an improved voting OCR (VOCR) algorithm. VOCR mitigates OCR variability by removing symbols (e.g., “dB,” “%”) and using tabulated data, generating multiple OCR candidates per cell and utilizing a voting mechanism to select reliable values. Our results indicate that VOCR achieves an image-level accuracy of 97.60% and high accuracy across all audiometric data categories, including PTA (99.95%), SRT (98.95%), WRS % (98.05%), and WRS stimulus (99.80%). The voting-based accuracy metric allows for the assessment of reliability, enabling a targeted review of areas with low consensus. This method has the potential to be employed in web-based data collection services, supporting real-time, standardized data management and reducing the need for manual extraction, making it a valuable tool for otolaryngological research.

technology.title: Identification of NUDT6 and LINGO1 as candidate genes for nCRT-associated signatures to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in rectal cancer patients
technology.desc: Rectal cancer is a highly prevalent cancer worldwide and a common cause of cancer death. Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT) is the first choice for advanced rectal cancer. In this study, we used bioinformatics approaches to explore candidate genes affected by nCRT in rectal cancer. A total of 26 samples of rectal cancer patients were collected and divided into the Treatment group (14 patients who received nCRT) and the Control group (12 patients who did not receive nCRT). candidate genes were selected by high-throughput sequencing, differential expression analysis, machine learning algorithms, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, and gene expression analysis. Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) was used to trace the enrichment pathways of these candidate genes. Additionally, the relationship between immune cells and these candidate genes was explored. A nomogram and molecular regulatory network were constructed based on the selected candidate genes. The quality of sequencing data was high for all samples. Overall, 35 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were discovered. Among them, NUDT6 and LINGO1 were identified as candidate genes with high discriminative ability (both with area under the curve (AUC) > 0.8). A nomogram with satisfactory exploratory performance was constructed. NUDT6 was significantly enriched in the ribosome and oxidative phosphorylation pathways, and was significantly positively correlated with Megakaryocyte-Erythroid Progenitor (MEP) and T helper cell 1 (Th1 cells), and significantly negatively correlated with Myocyte cells. LINGO1 was significantly enriched in the proteasome pathway and significantly positively correlated with Erythrocytes. Additionally, drug prediction analyses indicated that valproic acid was most highly associated with NUDT6, while bisphenol A is most closely linked to LINGO1. In this study, NUDT6 and LINGO1 were identified as potential candidate genes significantly associated with the Treatment group (patients who received nCRT) compared to the Control group (patients who did not). These findings may offer exploratory insights into the molecular correlates of nCRT treatment in rectal cancer. Moreover, as this study relies on a single-center convenience sample, these findings require further validation in multi-center prospective cohorts.
